items.t: How do I choose a lawyer in Georgia?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Choose a lawyer with experience in your type of case, who gives you an honest assessment of the risks and agrees the fee in advance and in writing. At MMLAW the first consultation is free, so you can meet the lawyer before deciding.

items.t: How much does the initial consultation cost?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: The initial consultation is free. We review your situation, explain your options and, if needed, propose terms for our engagement.

items.t: What documents should I bring?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Bring everything related to your case: ID, contracts, court decisions, notices, police or official reports and correspondence. If you don't have the documents, contact us anyway — we can help obtain them.

items.t: How long will my case take?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Every case is different. Some matters are settled through negotiation within weeks; court disputes can take months or longer. We give you a realistic estimate at the first consultation.

items.t: Do you work on a success-fee basis?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: In certain categories of cases — yes. The fee structure and amount are agreed in advance and in writing, so there are no hidden costs.

items.t: Which languages do you work in?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: We provide consultations and representation in Georgian, English and Russian — including for foreign nationals and international companies.

items.t: Where do you represent clients?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: We represent clients before courts of all instances in Georgia — district (city) courts, courts of appeal and the Supreme Court — as well as before administrative bodies and investigative authorities.

items.t: When do I have the right to a lawyer in Georgia?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
items.k: From the moment of arrest or of being charged — and before any questioning. You have the right to remain silent and to insist on your lawyer being present.

items.t: How long can I be held without a court decision?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
items.k: A person must be charged within 48 hours of arrest and brought before a court within the following 24 hours. If this doesn't happen, they must be released immediately.

items.t: What is a plea agreement?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
items.k: An agreement between the prosecution and the accused on guilt and sentence, which must be approved by the court. A defense lawyer's participation is mandatory. Never sign anything without independent legal advice.

items.t: When should I contact a criminal defense lawyer?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
items.k: As early as possible — ideally as soon as you are summoned for questioning, or during a search or arrest. Involving a lawyer early often decides the outcome: your lawyer helps you avoid mistakes when giving statements and protects your rights while evidence is gathered.

items.t: How much does a criminal defense lawyer cost?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
items.k: It depends on the complexity, stage and scope of the case. The first consultation is free — we assess the case and agree the fee with you in advance and in writing.

items.t: Can I refuse to give a statement?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
items.k: Yes. The accused has the right to remain silent — you can decline to answer questions and speak to a lawyer first.

items.t: Can a relative hire a lawyer for me?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
items.k: Yes. When someone is detained, it is often family members who find the lawyer. Call us or message us on WhatsApp — we'll tell you what to do first.

items.t: Am I entitled to a free lawyer?
items.d: Criminal defence lawyer — defence at every stage
items.k: If you can't pay, or your case is one of mandatory defence (for example a minor or a jury trial) and you have no private lawyer, the state pays for your defence through the Legal Aid Service.

items.t: Is using drugs a crime in Georgia?
items.d: Drug crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: The first time, in a small amount — as a rule, no. It is an administrative offence: a fine of GEL 500–2,000 or administrative detention of up to 60 days. If it happens again after an administrative penalty, it becomes a criminal offence.

items.t: What is the penalty for buying or possessing drugs?
items.d: Drug crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Under Article 260 of the Criminal Code — imprisonment of up to 6 years; for a large amount or other aggravating circumstances, 5 to 8 years; for an especially large amount or by an organised group, 8 to 20 years or life. Much depends on the amount and the evidence.

items.t: Is marijuana punished?
items.d: Drug crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Buying or possessing a small amount of marijuana is an administrative offence — a GEL 500 fine. Using it in public places, in front of minors or near schools carries higher fines. Large amounts and sale are criminal offences.

items.t: Can I refuse a drug test?
items.d: Drug crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Avoiding a test is itself an administrative offence — a fine of GEL 500–2,000 or administrative detention of up to 60 days. Call a lawyer before you decide.

items.t: If I hand drugs over voluntarily, am I liable?
items.d: Drug crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: By law, a person who voluntarily hands over the substance is released from criminal liability, unless the act contains another crime. It counts as voluntary only if declared before an investigation starts and the person actively helps with the seizure.

items.t: What other consequences can there be?
items.d: Drug crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Besides a criminal record, a court may take away certain rights, including the right to drive, under the Law on Combating Drug Crime.

items.t: What counts as cybercrime?
items.d: Cybercrime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Unauthorised access to a computer system, unlawful use or damage of data, and using tools designed for such acts. Fraud, extortion and threats committed online are criminal offences too.

items.t: I was scammed online. Can I get my money back?
items.d: Cybercrime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Sometimes, yes — especially if you act fast: contact your bank, keep all the evidence and talk to a lawyer. Don't trust services that promise to recover money for an upfront fee.

items.t: I'm being blackmailed with private photos. What should I do?
items.d: Cybercrime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Don't pay and stop replying, but don't delete anything. Contact a lawyer right away — blackmail and sharing private images are criminal offences.

items.t: Can the police take my phone?
items.d: Cybercrime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: As a rule, seizing a device and examining its contents requires a court order. Talk to your lawyer before signing any record or giving out passwords.

items.t: What is the difference between theft, open theft and robbery?
items.d: Property crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Theft is secret taking; open theft (ძარცვა) is taking openly, in front of others; robbery is an attack with violence dangerous to life or health, or the threat of it. Penalties get stricter in that order.

items.t: What counts as significant damage and a large amount?
items.d: Property crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: For property crimes, significant damage is a value over GEL 150, and a large amount is over GEL 10,000. Both make the penalty stricter.

items.t: I couldn't repay a debt. Is that fraud?
items.d: Property crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Not necessarily. Fraud requires an intent to deceive from the start. If an obligation simply wasn't met, it is often a civil dispute.

items.t: If I compensate the damage, will the case be dropped?
items.d: Property crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Compensation doesn't end the case automatically, but it can affect the sentence, the preventive measure or the terms of a plea agreement.

items.t: Is any tax debt a crime?
items.d: Economic crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: No. Criminal liability arises for intentional tax evasion where the amount exceeds GEL 100,000. Most disputes are resolved with the tax authority and in court.

items.t: I received a tax demand. What should I do?
items.d: Economic crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Contact a lawyer immediately. If within 45 working days of the demand the principal amount is paid, deferred or adjusted, there is no criminal liability.

items.t: What is money laundering?
items.d: Economic crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Giving illegal or unexplained property a lawful appearance to hide its real origin. The penalty is 3 to 6 years, up to 12 with aggravating circumstances.

items.t: I'm a company director. Am I liable?
items.d: Economic crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: That depends on who made which decisions and what they knew. A lawyer checks whether responsibility has been assigned correctly.

items.t: I was asked for a bribe. What should I do?
items.d: Corruption crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Don't pay, and contact a lawyer immediately. A bribe-giver is released from liability if they report it voluntarily — this step must be taken correctly.

items.t: What is the penalty for taking a bribe?
items.d: Corruption crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: 6 to 9 years' imprisonment; for a large amount (over GEL 10,000) 7 to 11 years; for an especially large amount (over GEL 30,000), repeatedly or by extortion, 11 to 15 years.

items.t: Who counts as an official?
items.d: Corruption crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Public servants and persons treated as such, including employees of public-law legal entities who exercise public powers.

items.t: I was secretly recorded. Is that evidence?
items.d: Corruption crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Only if it was obtained in the way the law requires, with the necessary authorisation. Checking this is one of the main tasks of the defence.

items.t: I was defending myself. Am I liable?
items.d: Violent crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: If it was lawful self-defence, the act is not unlawful. The question is whether the defence was clearly disproportionate to the attack. A lawyer proves this with evidence.

items.t: How is the severity of an injury decided?
items.d: Violent crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: By a medical examination. Minor, less serious and serious injuries fall under different articles — 1 to 3 years, 2 to 4 years and 4 to 7 years.

items.t: There was a fight and we were both hurt. What happens?
items.d: Violent crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: In such cases both sides can be both victim and accused. It is important that your version and evidence are recorded correctly from the start.

items.t: What is the penalty for homicide?
items.d: Violent crime lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Intentional homicide carries 10 to 15 years; with aggravating circumstances, 16 to 20 years or life imprisonment.

items.t: Is my child entitled to a free lawyer?
items.d: Juvenile lawyer in Georgia: legal help for minors
items.k: Yes. An accused minor and a minor victim are entitled to free legal aid at any stage of a criminal case if they have no private lawyer. A minor witness is entitled if unable to pay or in certain cases defined by law.

items.t: From what age is a person criminally liable in Georgia?
items.d: Juvenile lawyer in Georgia: legal help for minors
items.k: From 14. Special rules of the Juvenile Justice Code apply to persons under 18.

items.t: What is diversion?
items.d: Juvenile lawyer in Georgia: legal help for minors
items.k: Diversion allows a minor to avoid criminal prosecution by meeting certain conditions — for example mediation, community service or a rehabilitation programme. The decision is made by the prosecutor.

items.t: Can any lawyer defend a minor?
items.d: Juvenile lawyer in Georgia: legal help for minors
items.k: No. Under the Code, lawyers, judges, prosecutors and investigators working on juvenile cases must be specialised.

items.t: How are civil courts organised in Georgia?
items.d: Civil litigation lawyer in Georgia
items.k: First instance — district (city) courts; second instance — the Tbilisi and Kutaisi Courts of Appeal; the final, cassation instance — the Supreme Court of Georgia.

items.t: Can a dispute be resolved without going to court?
items.d: Civil litigation lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Yes — through negotiation, mediation or arbitration. For some categories of disputes (for example certain family, inheritance and neighbour disputes) court mediation may be mandatory.

items.t: How long do I have to file a claim?
items.d: Civil litigation lawyer in Georgia
items.k: It depends on the type of claim. Under the Civil Code of Georgia the general limitation period is 10 years, 3 years for contractual claims and 6 years for claims related to immovable property. Some claims have shorter periods, so it is best to act early.

items.t: What is the deadline to challenge an administrative act in court?
items.d: Administrative law lawyer in Georgia
items.k: As a rule, one month from the date the act was officially delivered to you. Some cases have different statutory terms, so check the exact deadline immediately.

items.t: Do I have to file an administrative complaint first?
items.d: Administrative law lawyer in Georgia
items.k: In some cases the law requires a complaint to the superior body before going to court; in others you may go straight to court. We assess which route is faster and stronger.

items.t: Can a fine be appealed?
items.d: Administrative law lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Yes. A decision on an administrative offence can be appealed to the superior body or to the court within short statutory deadlines.

items.t: What can I do if I was dismissed unlawfully?
items.d: Employment and labour lawyer in Georgia
items.k: You can ask your employer for the written grounds of dismissal and challenge it in court, seeking reinstatement or compensation. Deadlines are short (as a rule, 30 calendar days), so contact a lawyer immediately.

items.t: Is an oral employment contract valid?
items.d: Employment and labour lawyer in Georgia
items.k: An oral contract is possible, but a contract concluded for more than one month must be in writing.

items.t: Do you represent employees or employers?
items.d: Employment and labour lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Both. We help employees restore their rights, and help employers prevent disputes and represent them in court.

items.t: How long does it take to register a company in Georgia?
items.d: Corporate lawyer in Georgia
items.k: With properly prepared documents, registering an LLC with the National Agency of Public Registry usually takes one business day.

items.t: Can a foreigner own 100% of a Georgian company?
items.d: Corporate lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Yes. Foreign individuals and companies can be the sole founders of a Georgian LLC.

items.t: Which law governs companies in Georgia?
items.d: Corporate lawyer in Georgia
items.k: The Law of Georgia on Entrepreneurs (new version in force since 2022).

items.t: Where is property ownership registered?
items.d: Real estate lawyer in Georgia
items.k: At the National Agency of Public Registry (NAPR). Ownership of real estate arises upon registration. A registry extract shows the owner and any encumbrances (mortgage, seizure).

items.t: Can foreigners buy property in Georgia?
items.d: Real estate lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Yes. Foreigners can freely buy apartments, houses and non-agricultural land. Purchase of agricultural land by foreigners is restricted by law.

items.t: What should I check before buying?
items.d: Real estate lawyer in Georgia
items.k: The registry extract (owner, mortgage, seizure, prohibitions), the seller's authority, permits for new construction, and any utility or other debts.

items.t: Can we divorce without going to court?
items.d: Family and divorce lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Yes — if both spouses agree and there is no dispute over children or property, the divorce can be registered with the Civil Registry (through the Public Service Hall). Otherwise the divorce is decided by a court.

items.t: How is property divided?
items.d: Family and divorce lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Property acquired during the marriage is the spouses' joint property and is, as a rule, divided equally unless a marriage contract says otherwise. Property owned before marriage, gifts and inheritance remain personal property.

items.t: How is alimony determined?
items.d: Family and divorce lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Parents must support their minor children. The amount depends on the child's needs and the parents' financial situation — set by agreement or by the court.

items.t: How long do I have to accept an inheritance?
items.d: Inheritance lawyer in Georgia
items.k: 6 months from the opening of the inheritance — as a rule, the date of death. You can accept it by applying to a notary or by actually taking possession of the property.

items.t: Who are the first-line heirs?
items.d: Inheritance lawyer in Georgia
items.k: The deceased's children (including adopted children), spouse and parents. They inherit in equal shares unless a will provides otherwise.

items.t: What if I missed the 6-month deadline?
items.d: Inheritance lawyer in Georgia
items.k: If you missed it for a valid reason, a court can extend it. Whether you actually took possession of the property also matters. We'll assess your case.

items.t: Can a will be challenged?
items.d: Inheritance lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Yes — for example if the will's form was not respected or the testator was not aware of their actions when making it. Certain close relatives may also be entitled to a compulsory share regardless of the will.

items.t: Am I liable for the deceased's debts?
items.d: Inheritance lawyer in Georgia
items.k: As a rule, an heir is liable for debts only up to the value of the property inherited. It's worth checking the debts before accepting — if needed, you can renounce the inheritance.

items.t: Is there inheritance tax in Georgia?
items.d: Inheritance lawyer in Georgia
items.k: There is no separate inheritance tax. First- and second-order heirs — children, spouse, parents, siblings — pay no tax on property received by inheritance or gift. Third- and fourth-order heirs (grandparents, uncles, aunts) are exempt up to GEL 150,000 a year. Otherwise the value is taxed as income at 20%.

items.t: Where are trademarks registered in Georgia?
items.d: Intellectual property lawyer in Georgia
items.k: With Sakpatenti — the National Intellectual Property Center of Georgia. International registration is possible through the Madrid system.

items.t: How long does trademark protection last?
items.d: Intellectual property lawyer in Georgia
items.k: 10 years from the filing date, renewable every 10 years.

items.t: Does copyright need to be registered?
items.d: Intellectual property lawyer in Georgia
items.k: No — copyright arises automatically when a work is created. Depositing the work with Sakpatenti helps prove authorship.

items.t: Is failing to repay a debt fraud?
items.d: Fraud lawyer in Georgia — defence and recovery
items.k: Not necessarily. Fraud requires intent to deceive from the start. If an obligation simply wasn't met, it is often a civil dispute.

items.t: I was scammed — can I get my money back?
items.d: Fraud lawyer in Georgia — defence and recovery
items.k: The earlier you act, the better the chances: a police report, freezing the suspect's property and the compensation mechanism. In large-scale cases the convicted person is ordered to pay compensation.

items.t: What is the penalty for fraud?
items.d: Fraud lawyer in Georgia — defence and recovery
items.k: For the basic offence — from a fine up to 4 years in prison; with aggravating circumstances — up to 10 years.

items.t: Which crimes does compensation cover?
items.d: Victims of financial crime — getting the money back
items.k: For example: large-scale fraud, extortion and embezzlement, property damage over GEL 10,000, abuse of authority in a company and large-scale computer crime.

items.t: What if the convicted person leaves the country?
items.d: Victims of financial crime — getting the money back
items.k: If they are a Georgian citizen or a person with status in Georgia, they are banned from leaving until compensation is paid — unless you waive it in writing.

items.t: Can I also file a civil claim?
items.d: Victims of financial crime — getting the money back
items.k: Yes. Compensation doesn't take away your right to a civil claim — you just can't claim again the part you already received.

items.t: How long do I have to appeal a tax decision?
items.d: Tax lawyer in Georgia — disputes and tax crimes
items.k: 30 days from receiving it. Complaints are usually filed electronically.

items.t: Can tax debt be reduced?
items.d: Tax lawyer in Georgia — disputes and tax crimes
items.k: Yes, in cases set by law a tax settlement can be signed with the Revenue Service to reduce part of the debt.

items.t: My bank suspended a transaction — what should I do?
items.d: Money laundering defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Ask for a written explanation and prepare documents proving where the money came from. If it reaches an investigation, involve a lawyer straight away.

items.t: What is unexplained property?
items.d: Money laundering defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Property for which the person or their relatives have no documents proving it was lawfully obtained.

items.t: What is the penalty for money laundering?
items.d: Money laundering defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: For the basic offence — a fine or 3 to 6 years; on an especially large scale or by an organised group — up to 12 years.

items.t: Is 'renting out' my account or card risky?
items.d: Money laundering defence lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Yes. If someone else's money comes into your account and you transfer or withdraw it, you may end up accused as a participant in fraud or of money laundering — even if you only took a 'small fee'.

items.t: My account has been frozen — what should I do?
items.d: Asset freezing and confiscation lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Find out in which case and on what grounds. The court order can be appealed — contact a lawyer straight away.

items.t: Can a family member's property be frozen?
items.d: Asset freezing and confiscation lawyer in Georgia
items.k: It can, if they are treated as a person connected to the accused. Then it is important to prove the property was obtained lawfully and independently.

items.t: What is the difference between a freeze and confiscation?
items.d: Asset freezing and confiscation lawyer in Georgia
items.k: A freeze is temporary — it restricts dealing with the property. Confiscation is final: the property passes to the state.

items.t: Can a private company director be liable?
items.d: Abuse of office and exceeding authority — lawyer
items.k: Not under Article 332, but possibly under Article 220 — if they used their authority against the company's interests for gain and caused significant damage.

items.t: Is every mistake at work a crime?
items.d: Abuse of office and exceeding authority — lawyer
items.k: No. There must be a substantial breach of rights or interests, and for abuse of authority also an aim of gain or advantage.

items.t: Is every customs violation a crime?
items.d: Smuggling and customs offences — lawyer in Georgia
items.k: No. Criminal liability requires a large amount — a customs value over GEL 15,000 (over GEL 5,000 for goods in a cache). Smaller violations are usually dealt with in a different way.

items.t: I forgot to declare gold jewellery — what happens?
items.d: Smuggling and customs offences — lawyer in Georgia
items.k: Moving precious-metal jewellery in breach of the rules is punished under a separate part of Article 214. The circumstances matter a lot — contact a lawyer straight away.

items.t: What is the penalty for smuggling?
items.d: Smuggling and customs offences — lawyer in Georgia
items.k: For a large amount — a fine or 3 to 5 years; with aggravating circumstances — up to 15 years.

items.t: Is a director personally liable for an LLC's debts?
items.d: Director liability and company insolvency in Georgia
items.k: Generally no — the company is liable with its own assets. But a director can be liable if they breached their duties and caused damage, or if a crime is established.

items.t: The company can't pay its debts — what should I do?
items.d: Director liability and company insolvency in Georgia
items.k: Assess the situation with a lawyer as early as possible: rehabilitation or an agreement with creditors may be better than liquidation.

items.t: I'm a creditor — how do I protect my claim?
items.d: Director liability and company insolvency in Georgia
items.k: Register the claim in the insolvency case on time and, if needed, ask the court for interim measures.

items.t: How many grams of marijuana is a crime in Georgia?
items.d: Drug possession lawyer in Georgia — Article 260
items.k: Up to and including 5 grams of dried marijuana is a small amount — a GEL 500 administrative fine. More than 5 grams is already a criminal case under Article 260; over 70 grams is a large amount, over 250 grams especially large.

items.t: What is the penalty under Article 260, Part 1?
items.d: Drug possession lawyer in Georgia — Article 260
items.k: Up to 6 years in prison. Part 2 — 5 to 8 years; Part 3 — 8 to 20 years or life.

items.t: Is the quantity counted with packaging or fillers?
items.d: Drug possession lawyer in Georgia — Article 260
items.k: No. By law the quantity is the pure substance, without fillers. That is why checking the lab report matters so much.

items.t: How do I get a criminal record certificate?
items.d: Removing a criminal record in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: The certificate is issued by the MIA Service Agency — online on its website or app, or at a branch; GEL 20, 3 working days. For use abroad it usually needs an apostille. If the certificate still shows a conviction, we check whether it has expired and whether it can be removed early.

items.t: When will my criminal record expire?
items.d: Removing a criminal record in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: It depends on the sentence and the category of crime: for a suspended sentence — after the probation period; for a sentence lighter than imprisonment — 1 year after serving it; for imprisonment — 3, 6 or 8 years after serving it.

items.t: Can a criminal record be removed early?
items.d: Removing a criminal record in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Yes. If you have behaved impeccably since serving the sentence, a court can remove the record at your request before the period ends.

items.t: What does a removed record mean?
items.d: Removing a criminal record in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: An expired or removed record is no longer taken into account — for example, when a new case is classified or a sentence is set.

items.t: When is early release possible?
items.d: Early release on parole in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: For a less serious crime — after half of the sentence, for a serious crime — two-thirds, for an especially serious crime — three-quarters. In every case at least 6 months must be served.

items.t: Who decides?
items.d: Early release on parole in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: For imprisonment — the local board of the Special Penitentiary Service; for other sentences — a court.

items.t: Can the family hire a lawyer?
items.d: Early release on parole in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Yes. A family member can contact us; we meet the prisoner and prepare the case.

items.t: I lost money in a pyramid scheme — can I get it back?
items.d: Pyramid schemes and investment fraud in Georgia
items.k: The earlier you act, the better the chances: a report, a freeze on property and the compensation mechanism. In large-scale fraud the convicted person is ordered to pay compensation.

items.t: I brought friends into the scheme — am I liable?
items.d: Pyramid schemes and investment fraud in Georgia
items.k: If you didn't know the scheme was a deception, that is the core of your defence. Talk to a lawyer before giving a statement to investigators.

items.t: The platform is abroad — what can be done?
items.d: Pyramid schemes and investment fraud in Georgia
items.k: A case can be opened in Georgia if the victim or the recipient of the money is here; international cooperation is used where needed. Contacting your bank quickly matters too.

items.t: If I pay, will they stop?
items.d: Blackmail with private photos in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Often not. Paying shows the pressure works, and demands grow. It is better to keep the evidence and contact a lawyer and the police.

items.t: The photo has already been posted — can it be removed?
items.d: Blackmail with private photos in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Yes. We use platforms' takedown tools and, where needed, legal routes — while the criminal case continues.

items.t: Will my name appear anywhere?
items.d: Blackmail with private photos in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: We work in complete confidence. There are also ways to protect a victim's private life during the investigation and in court — your lawyer will ask for them.

items.t: How long until a loan is time-barred?
items.d: Time-barred loans in Georgia: limitation period and defence
items.k: The limitation period for a loan claim is 3 years, 6 years for contracts concerning real estate. If a court has already confirmed the debt — 10 years.

items.t: Is a time-barred loan cancelled automatically?
items.d: Time-barred loans in Georgia: limitation period and defence
items.k: No. After the period expires the debtor may refuse to pay, but must raise it in court themselves. The court does not apply the time bar on its own initiative.

items.t: A collector asked me to pay a small amount — what should I do?
items.d: Time-barred loans in Georgia: limitation period and defence
items.k: Check the period before you pay. Paying part of the debt or interest, or acknowledging it, restarts the limitation period.

items.t: Does a time-barred loan stay in my credit history?
items.d: Time-barred loans in Georgia: limitation period and defence
items.k: According to the National Bank's financial education portal, a time-barred debt stays in the credit history for 5 years, after which you can ask for it to be removed.

items.t: How long does a restraining order last?
items.d: Restraining and protective orders in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Up to 1 month. A protective order is issued by a court for up to 9 months and can be extended by 3 more.

items.t: Can a restraining order be appealed?
items.d: Restraining and protective orders in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Yes. Both the victim and the person it was issued against can appeal within 3 days of receiving it. The deadline is very short — contact a lawyer immediately.

items.t: What happens if an order is breached?
items.d: Restraining and protective orders in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Breaching an order is a crime: a fine, community service or up to 1 year in prison; repeatedly — 1 to 3 years.

items.t: Is the order cancelled after reconciliation?
items.d: Restraining and protective orders in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Not automatically. It can be cancelled on a joint application if the victim or other family members are no longer at risk.

items.t: My account was seized — how do I find out why?
items.d: Removing a seizure on bank accounts and property in Georgia
items.k: A seizure is imposed within an enforcement case. We can check the case, the creditor and the amount, and tell you the fastest way to lift it.

items.t: The tax office put an „inkaso“ on my account — what does it mean?
items.d: Removing a seizure on bank accounts and property in Georgia
items.k: It is a collection order: the Revenue Service takes the amount of a confirmed tax debt from your account. If you disagree with the debt, you can appeal — while the dispute lasts, the obligation to pay is suspended.

items.t: Can my salary be seized too?
items.d: Removing a seizure on bank accounts and property in Georgia
items.k: By law money can be collected from salary and other income, but income below the subsistence minimum and targeted state assistance are protected from seizure.

items.t: A seizure from an old case is still active — what can I do?
items.d: Removing a seizure on bank accounts and property in Georgia
items.k: If 10 years have passed since enforcement proceedings for a money claim began, enforcement must end and the seizure be lifted — except in cases set by law, such as alimony.

items.t: How long do I have to appeal an enforcement officer's action?
items.d: Removing a seizure on bank accounts and property in Georgia
items.k: 15 calendar days from the action — to the head of the National Bureau of Enforcement.

items.t: What is the difference between a pardon and an amnesty?
items.d: Presidential pardon and amnesty in Georgia — how to apply
items.k: A pardon is granted by the President to a specific person on request. An amnesty is declared by Parliament through a law and applies to everyone who meets its conditions.

items.t: Who can request a pardon?
items.d: Presidential pardon and amnesty in Georgia — how to apply
items.k: The convicted person or a family member. The Pardon Commission reviews the request and the President decides.

items.t: Is there an amnesty in 2026?
items.d: Presidential pardon and amnesty in Georgia — how to apply
items.k: An amnesty can only be declared by a law passed by Parliament. If such a law is adopted, we will check whether it covers your article and sentence.

items.t: How long will I lose my licence for drink-driving?
items.d: Driving licence suspension in Georgia: 6 months, 1, 3 years
items.k: At 0.3–0.7‰ — 6 months; over 0.7‰ or refusing the test — 1 year. With minor damage — 3 years and a GEL 2,000 fine.

items.t: Will my licence be suspended for an unpaid fine?
items.d: Driving licence suspension in Georgia: 6 months, 1, 3 years
items.k: Yes. If a traffic fine isn't paid within 30 days, and then within another 30 days with a surcharge, the licence is suspended.

items.t: Can I appeal?
items.d: Driving licence suspension in Georgia: 6 months, 1, 3 years
items.k: Yes. The decision can be appealed within 10 days of receiving it. A lawyer checks the test procedure, the record and the video.

items.t: Do I need to retake the exam afterwards?
items.d: Driving licence suspension in Georgia: 6 months, 1, 3 years
items.k: After a suspension for an unpaid fine, the licence is restored when the term ends and no exam is required. In other cases the rule needs to be checked.

items.t: How long do I have to appeal a fine?
items.d: Appealing a fine in Georgia: camera, patrol, parking
items.k: 10 days from receiving the decision. If you missed it for a valid reason, you can ask for the deadline to be restored.

items.t: Can a parking or bus-lane fine be appealed too?
items.d: Appealing a fine in Georgia: camera, patrol, parking
items.k: Yes. These are administrative offences too — for example, breaking parking rules in Tbilisi falls under Article 125² — and the decision can be appealed within 10 days of receipt.

items.t: Do I have to pay while appealing?
items.d: Appealing a fine in Georgia: camera, patrol, parking
items.k: An appeal pauses the payment deadline until it is decided. If it is rejected, the fine must be paid.

items.t: Someone else was driving my car — what should I do?
items.d: Appealing a fine in Georgia: camera, patrol, parking
items.k: That is a common ground for appeal. Say who was driving and provide evidence.

items.t: When can I claim moral damage?
items.d: Compensation for moral damage in Georgia
items.k: Only in cases set by law — for example, injury, culpable harm to honour, dignity or private life, or unlawful detention or conviction.

items.t: How much will a court award?
items.d: Compensation for moral damage in Georgia
items.k: There is no fixed rate. The court sets a 'reasonable and fair' amount based on the severity of the harm, fault and practice.

items.t: I was unlawfully detained — am I owed compensation?
items.d: Compensation for moral damage in Georgia
items.k: A rehabilitated person is compensated by the state for damage from unlawful conviction or detention — regardless of officials' fault.

items.t: How is paternity established in court?
items.d: Establishing paternity in court in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Mainly by DNA testing. If that's impossible, the court considers living together, raising or supporting the child together, and other evidence of acknowledgment.

items.t: Who can apply to establish paternity?
items.d: Establishing paternity in court in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: A parent, the child's guardian, the person supporting the child, or the child after reaching adulthood.

items.t: Can child support be claimed too?
items.d: Establishing paternity in court in Georgia — lawyer
items.k: Yes. Once paternity is established, the child has the same rights as a child of married parents — including the right to support.

items.t: Can I take my child abroad without the other parent's consent?
items.d: Taking a child abroad from Georgia: parental consent
items.k: By law, for temporary travel of a child under 16, one parent's permission and an adult escort are enough. But a passport usually needs both parents' consent, and in a dispute a court decides.

items.t: The other parent won't consent to a passport — what can I do?
items.d: Taking a child abroad from Georgia: parental consent
items.k: In some cases one parent's consent is enough (e.g. the other parent's whereabouts are unknown or travel is needed for treatment). Otherwise you can go to court.

items.t: The other parent took our child abroad and won't return them — what should I do?
items.d: Taking a child abroad from Georgia: parental consent
items.k: If the child is in a Hague Convention country, you can ask for the child's return. Act quickly — time matters a lot in these cases.

items.t: How long do I have to challenge a dismissal?
items.d: Unfair dismissal in Georgia — how to challenge it
items.k: The deadlines are very short: ask for written reasons within 30 days, then sue within 30 days of receiving them. If you didn't ask for reasons, you have 30 days from receiving the dismissal notice.

items.t: Can a pregnant woman be dismissed?
items.d: Unfair dismissal in Georgia — how to challenge it
items.k: Dismissal is prohibited from notifying the employer of pregnancy until the end of maternity and childcare leave — except in cases listed by law, such as the end of a fixed term, resignation or a serious breach of duties.

items.t: What compensation do I get for redundancy?
items.d: Unfair dismissal in Georgia — how to challenge it
items.k: With 30 days' written notice — at least 1 month's salary; with 3 days' notice — at least 2 months' salary. Pay for unused leave comes on top.

items.t: Can I be dismissed during probation?
items.d: Unfair dismissal in Georgia — how to challenge it
items.k: Yes. A probation period (up to 6 months) can be ended at any time and the Article 48 rules don't apply unless the contract says otherwise. The time worked must still be paid.

items.t: How many days of leave am I entitled to?
items.d: Labour Code of Georgia: leave, maternity, salary
items.k: At least 24 working days of paid leave and at least 15 calendar days of unpaid leave a year. A contract can give more, never less.

items.t: How long is maternity leave?
items.d: Labour Code of Georgia: leave, maternity, salary
items.k: 126 days for pregnancy and childbirth (143 with complications or twins), then childcare leave. In total 183 days (or 200) are paid, by the state.

items.t: My salary is late — what can I do?
items.d: Labour Code of Georgia: leave, maternity, salary
items.k: For every day of delay the employer owes you 0.07% of the amount. Send a written demand; if there's no agreement within 14 days, you can go to court.

items.t: Is overtime paid?
items.d: Labour Code of Georgia: leave, maternity, salary
items.k: Yes — at an increased hourly rate agreed by the parties, or with extra time off by agreement. Pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, parents of children under 3 and minors can't be made to work overtime without their consent.

items.t: How do I find out if I'm on the debtors' register?
items.d: Debtors' register in Georgia: checking and removal
items.k: The register's data are public. The National Bureau of Enforcement issues an extract no later than the next working day after the application, for a fee. We can check which case and which creditor you're registered for.

items.t: I paid the debt — will I be removed automatically?
items.d: Debtors' register in Georgia: checking and removal
items.k: Paying in full is a ground for removal, and all restrictions are lifted on removal. If the entry hasn't been removed, you need to contact the enforcement officer — we can help.

items.t: I'm on the register — can I sell my flat?
items.d: Debtors' register in Georgia: checking and removal
items.k: Only with consent: in cases for the state budget — the National Bureau of Enforcement's; in other cases — the Bureau's and the creditor's.

items.t: I'm on the register for a very old debt — what can I do?
items.d: Debtors' register in Georgia: checking and removal
items.k: If 10 years have passed since enforcement of a money claim began, enforcement must end and you must be removed — except in cases set by law, such as alimony.

items.t: The flat is in my spouse's name — is it still joint?
items.d: Dividing marital property in a Georgian divorce
items.k: If it was bought during the marriage, yes — whoever it's registered to, unless a marriage contract says otherwise.

items.t: Is a flat bought before marriage divided?
items.d: Dividing marital property in a Georgian divorce
items.k: Usually not — it's personal property. But if its value grew significantly through joint spending during the marriage (renovation, completing construction), a court may treat it as joint.

items.t: How long do I have to ask for division?
items.d: Dividing marital property in a Georgian divorce
items.k: After divorce the limitation period is 3 years. When it starts running can be disputed, so don't delay.

items.t: Who pays the mortgage after division?
items.d: Dividing marital property in a Georgian divorce
items.k: Joint debts are split between the spouses in proportion to their shares of joint property. With the bank, though, the loan contract still applies — so this needs to be settled separately in the agreement or lawsuit.

items.t: Is a handwritten will valid?
items.d: Wills in Georgia — making and challenging a will
items.k: Yes — a handwritten will is valid if the testator wrote it by hand and signed it. But it is easier to contest, so we recommend a notarial will.

items.t: Can I leave my child nothing at all?
items.d: Wills in Georgia — making and challenging a will
items.k: Children, parents and the spouse are entitled to a compulsory share regardless of the will — half of their share under the law. The exception is when an heir has lost the right to inherit under the law, for example as an unworthy heir.

items.t: How long do I have to challenge a will?
items.d: Wills in Georgia — making and challenging a will
items.k: 2 years from the inheritance opening. After that, the will can no longer be challenged.

items.t: There are several wills — which one applies?
items.d: Wills in Georgia — making and challenging a will
items.k: A newer will revokes the older one to the extent they conflict. A notarial will, however, takes priority and cannot be revoked by a will in another form.

items.t: I lent money without an IOU — can I get it back?
items.d: Debt recovery in Georgia — loans, IOUs, enforcement
items.k: Possibly. Evidence can be a bank transfer, messages, an audio recording or a witness. The sooner you contact us, the more evidence we can preserve.

items.t: How long do I have to claim the debt?
items.d: Debt recovery in Georgia — loans, IOUs, enforcement
items.k: The limitation period is 3 years — usually from the repayment date. After that the debtor can rely on the limitation period and the court will reject the claim.

items.t: How much does a lawsuit cost?
items.d: Debt recovery in Georgia — loans, IOUs, enforcement
items.k: The court fee is 3% of the amount claimed, but at least 100 GEL. If you win, the losing party usually reimburses the court costs.

items.t: The debtor has no assets — what happens?
items.d: Debt recovery in Georgia — loans, IOUs, enforcement
items.k: The judgment goes to enforcement and the debtor is entered into the debtors register: they can't register new property or a car without the enforcement bureau finding out. Money can also be deducted from their salary.

items.t: Is a verbal agreement a contract?
items.d: Contract drafting and review in Georgia
items.k: Often — yes, if the law doesn't require a particular form. But a verbal agreement is hard to prove. Real estate, however, can only be acquired with a written contract and registration.

items.t: Do I need to have a contract certified by a notary?
items.d: Contract drafting and review in Georgia
items.k: Not always. Notarisation is required by law in some cases and useful in others: for example, a debt under a notarised loan agreement can be recovered even without going to court.

items.t: How high can a contractual penalty be?
items.d: Contract drafting and review in Georgia
items.k: The parties set it freely, but the agreement must be in writing. If the penalty is excessive, a court can reduce it; for loans, the law sets a cap.

items.t: Is a contract in English valid?
items.d: Contract drafting and review in Georgia
items.k: Yes, a contract can be made in any language. You may need a Georgian translation for the Public Registry or a court, so we often prepare a bilingual text.

items.t: Who can apply to the court?
items.d: Banning a family member from gambling in Georgia
items.k: A parent, spouse, child or someone who lives permanently with the person.

items.t: How much does it cost and how long does it take?
items.d: Banning a family member from gambling in Georgia
items.k: The application is free of court fees. The judge issues an order within 3–5 working days and it takes effect immediately.

items.t: Does the ban cover online casinos?
items.d: Banning a family member from gambling in Georgia
items.k: Yes. It covers casinos, slot halls, betting and online gambling — when the operator holds a Georgian permit.

items.t: Can a person ban themselves?
items.d: Banning a family member from gambling in Georgia
items.k: Yes — by applying to the Revenue Service. They are also listed for 5 years.

items.t: Who is barred from gambling by law?
items.d: Banning a family member from gambling in Georgia
items.k: Georgian citizens under 25, foreigners under 18, people employed in public institutions, the National Bank and regulators, and family members registered in the database of socially vulnerable families.

items.t: Can my spouse's gambling debt be collected from our flat?
items.d: Gambling debts in Georgia — protecting family property
items.k: Only from their share. Joint property can be used only if a court finds the money served the family's common interests. Money lost gambling usually doesn't.

items.t: Is a loan taken for gambling void?
items.d: Gambling debts in Georgia — protecting family property
items.k: No — the purpose of a loan doesn't affect its validity. But interest and penalties above the legal limits can be reduced, and you can refuse to pay a time-barred debt.

items.t: Am I liable for my child's debt?
items.d: Gambling debts in Georgia — protecting family property
items.k: No, unless you are a guarantor or co-borrower. An adult child's debt is collected only from their own property.

items.t: How do I stop new debts?
items.d: Gambling debts in Georgia — protecting family property
items.k: A family member applies to the court to place the person on the dependent list — after that they cannot gamble at any licensed casino or betting operator for 5 years.

items.t: Is girao legal?
items.d: Living in a flat for a lump sum (girao) in Georgia
items.k: Yes — the law expressly allows a home to secure a loan when it is handed to the lender to live in. The key is a notarised contract and a mortgage registered in the registry.

items.t: What if the owner doesn't give my money back?
items.d: Living in a flat for a lump sum (girao) in Georgia
items.k: If the mortgage is registered, you recover the money from the flat through enforcement. Without registration you are an ordinary creditor, in line with everyone else.

items.t: Is a notary required?
items.d: Living in a flat for a lump sum (girao) in Georgia
items.k: Yes. A mortgage securing a loan must be notarised, and it takes effect only when registered in the Public Registry.

items.t: The flat already has a bank mortgage — can I still do girao?
items.d: Living in a flat for a lump sum (girao) in Georgia
items.k: You can, but the bank has priority and gets paid first. We advise against it, or recommend extra protection terms.

items.t: Does a lease need a notary?
items.d: Renting an apartment in Georgia — the lease
items.k: No. But to register the lease, signatures must be certified or both parties must sign at the registry.

items.t: The flat was sold — do I have to move out?
items.d: Renting an apartment in Georgia — the lease
items.k: No. If the flat was already handed to you, the new owner takes over the lease.

items.t: What tax does the landlord pay?
items.d: Renting an apartment in Georgia — the lease
items.k: An individual renting out housing for living purposes without claiming expenses pays 5% of the rent.

items.t: Can the lease be in English or Russian?
items.d: Renting an apartment in Georgia — the lease
items.k: Yes. We usually prepare a bilingual text — Georgian plus English or Russian — for the registry and courts.

items.t: Can I borrow from a private person against my flat?
items.d: Mortgage in Georgia — contract, registration, enforcement
items.k: As an individual, generally not — only a supervised or registered lender can make loans secured by real estate. Girao is the exception.

items.t: Can the flat pass to the creditor automatically?
items.d: Mortgage in Georgia — contract, registration, enforcement
items.k: No. Ownership passes only on a joint application by owner and creditor; otherwise the money is recovered through enforcement.

items.t: My loan has very high interest — what can I do?
items.d: Mortgage in Georgia — contract, registration, enforcement
items.k: The effective annual rate must not exceed 50%, and the law caps penalties and charges. You can refuse to pay the excess — we'll check the contract.

items.t: Is systematic registration still free?
items.d: Land registration in Georgia — sporadic and occupied land
items.k: No. The systematic registration reform ended on 1 January 2026. Land is now registered on your own application, by the sporadic procedure.

items.t: I have no documents — can I register my land?
items.d: Land registration in Georgia — sporadic and occupied land
items.k: Possibly. The law accepts many old documents — from household books to land-tax lists. For self-occupied land, witness testimony can also count.

items.t: How much does land registration cost?
items.d: Land registration in Georgia — sporadic and occupied land
items.k: Agricultural land — GEL 50 (300 in Tbilisi and Batumi), non-agricultural — GEL 300, plus surveying. Self-occupied land — GEL 600.

items.t: My neighbour's plot overlaps mine — what now?
items.d: Land registration in Georgia — sporadic and occupied land
items.k: First notary mediation, within 3 weeks. If you can't agree, a court decides. We prepare the boundary evidence and represent you.

items.t: Can I build a house on agricultural land?
items.d: Building a house on agricultural land in Georgia
items.k: On a private plot — often yes, if it fits the zone or surrounding buildings. Outside settlements, no permit is issued for housing. We'll check your plot.

items.t: Who changes land designation?
items.d: Building a house on agricultural land in Georgia
items.k: The Public Registry — where there is a justified need, based on a commission's opinion.

items.t: What does a change of designation cost?
items.d: Building a house on agricultural land in Georgia
items.k: The registration fee is GEL 50. Compensation applies only in Tbilisi and Batumi (GEL 34,001/ha) and special-regulation territories (GEL 100,000/ha).

items.t: Can I bring Lyrica (pregabalin) into Georgia?
items.d: Bringing medication into Georgia — what is restricted
items.k: Yes, for treatment — with medical documents and a customs declaration. Without documents a criminal case can start, because pregabalin is controlled in Georgia.

items.t: Customs took my medicine — what should I do?
items.d: Bringing medication into Georgia — what is restricted
items.k: Don't give a statement without a lawyer and keep all documents. We check which article applies and work to close the case if the medicine was for your treatment.

items.t: I'm only in transit — does this apply to me?
items.d: Bringing medication into Georgia — what is restricted
items.k: Yes. The law covers people in transit too: carry the medicine with medical and customs documents.

items.t: How much Lyrica is a crime?
items.d: Lyrica (pregabalin) and tramadol in Georgia — Article 261
items.k: More than 0.6 g of pregabalin is already a criminal case; a large amount is over 6 g. The medicine form counts, so a few capsules can be enough.

items.t: I have a prescription — is it still a crime?
items.d: Lyrica (pregabalin) and tramadol in Georgia — Article 261
items.k: Medicine prescribed by a doctor and lawfully obtained is not a crime. Keep the prescription and proof of purchase.

items.t: What is the penalty for tramadol?
items.d: Lyrica (pregabalin) and tramadol in Georgia — Article 261
items.k: Basic — a fine or corrective labour up to 1 year; in a large amount — 3 to 7 years; especially large — 7 to 12 years.

items.t: I gave some to a friend for free — is that dealing?
items.d: Drug dealing charges in Georgia — Articles 260²–260⁴
items.k: Free transfer is a separate crime (Article 260²) — 3 to 8 years for marijuana, 10 to 15 years for other narcotic drugs.

items.t: How is keeping different from dealing?
items.d: Drug dealing charges in Georgia — Articles 260²–260⁴
items.k: Keeping falls under Article 260 and is punished less severely; for dealing, the prosecution must prove a sale or transfer. That is often the key issue for the defence.

items.t: What rights does a convicted person lose?
items.d: Drug dealing charges in Georgia — Articles 260²–260⁴
items.k: A dealer loses the listed rights for 15 years, and medical and pharmaceutical work for 20 years. A plea agreement can reduce this.

items.t: The positive result is wrong — what can I do?
items.d: Drug test in Georgia — can you refuse? Fines and rights
items.k: Within 10 days ask for an alternative test of the sealed control sample, and contact us — the result can also be challenged in court.

items.t: Will I lose my driving licence?
items.d: Drug test in Georgia — can you refuse? Fines and rights
items.k: A court takes away the driving licence of a person punished for drug use for 3 years.

items.t: How many grams of cocaine is a crime?
items.d: Cocaine, MDMA, amphetamine in Georgia — amounts and penalties
items.k: Up to 0.06 g is a small amount — an administrative case. Above 0.06 g it's a criminal case, above 0.6 g a large amount (5 to 8 years), above 2 g especially large (8 to 20 years or life).

items.t: How many ecstasy pills count as a large amount?
items.d: Cocaine, MDMA, amphetamine in Georgia — amounts and penalties
items.k: A large amount is 0.5 g of MDMA, and the MDMA content of a pill varies — the forensic examination establishes it. So even a few pills can count as a large amount.

items.t: How much 'spice' is a crime?
items.d: Cocaine, MDMA, amphetamine in Georgia — amounts and penalties
items.k: Any amount of a new psychoactive substance is a crime — up to 6 years in prison.

items.t: I'm a foreigner — what happens?
items.d: Cocaine, MDMA, amphetamine in Georgia — amounts and penalties
items.k: The rules are the same. You have the right to an interpreter and a lawyer; don't sign anything you don't understand. We work in English and Russian.

items.t: Do I pay tax on money from Upwork or Fiverr?
items.d: Freelancer tax in Georgia: Upwork, Fiverr, foreign salary
items.k: Yes, if you do the work in Georgia. As a sole trader with small business status — 1%; unregistered — 20% through an annual return.

items.t: How do I register as a sole trader?
items.d: Freelancer tax in Georgia: Upwork, Fiverr, foreign salary
items.k: At the Public Service Hall, with your ID and an address. Then you apply for small business status to the Revenue Service on rs.ge.

items.t: What is the 1% limit?
items.d: Freelancer tax in Georgia: Upwork, Fiverr, foreign salary
items.k: GEL 500,000 a year. Above it, all income is taxed at 3% from that month to the end of the year; if you exceed it 2 years in a row, the status is cancelled.

items.t: Can a foreign salary be taxed at 1%?
items.d: Freelancer tax in Georgia: Upwork, Fiverr, foreign salary
items.k: No. Salary is excluded from the 1%. If you genuinely provide services rather than work as an employee, the contract must show it — we review the contract.

items.t: What if I don't file the annual return?
items.d: Freelancer tax in Georgia: Upwork, Fiverr, foreign salary
items.k: The penalty is 5% of the tax, 10% if more than 2 months late, plus interest of 0.05% per day.

items.t: Do we withhold tax for a remote employee living abroad?
items.d: Freelancer tax in Georgia: Upwork, Fiverr, foreign salary
items.k: For services performed abroad, as a rule, no; for management and financial services — 10%. Salary depends on the details — contact us before signing the contract.

items.t: How do I get a criminal record certificate online?
items.d: Criminal record certificate in Georgia — fee, apostille
items.k: On the MIA Service Agency website or app, after registering. It costs GEL 20 and takes 3 working days.

items.t: How long is the certificate valid?
items.d: Criminal record certificate in Georgia — fee, apostille
items.k: 15 calendar days.

items.t: Can someone else get it for me?
items.d: Criminal record certificate in Georgia — fee, apostille
items.k: Yes — with your written consent or a power of attorney.

items.t: The certificate shows an old conviction — what can I do?
items.d: Criminal record certificate in Georgia — fee, apostille
items.k: We check whether it has expired. If not, it may be possible to have it removed early through the court.

items.t: Does Georgia extradite to the US?
items.d: Does Georgia extradite? Extradition lawyer in Tbilisi
items.k: There is no extradition treaty in force between Georgia and the US that we know of; extradition then needs a separate agreement for the individual case, and every refusal ground still applies. Georgian citizens are not extradited.

items.t: Does Georgia extradite to the UK?
items.d: Does Georgia extradite? Extradition lawyer in Tbilisi
items.k: Yes, it can — both are parties to the European Convention on Extradition. A court reviews each request, and the grounds for refusal apply.

items.t: Is Georgia a non-extradition country?
items.d: Does Georgia extradite? Extradition lawyer in Tbilisi
items.k: No. Georgia does extradite foreigners in some cases, including to Russia; only its own citizens are protected. Each case turns on the treaty, the charge and the refusal grounds.

items.t: How long can I be held pending extradition?
items.d: Does Georgia extradite? Extradition lawyer in Tbilisi
items.k: Up to 9 months in total — 3 months, extendable twice. Bail or another milder measure is possible.

items.t: Am I entitled to a free interpreter?
items.d: Foreigner arrested in Georgia: rights and first steps
items.k: Yes. If you don't speak Georgian, the state provides an interpreter, and a lawyer is also mandatory.

items.t: Will my consulate be informed?
items.d: Foreigner arrested in Georgia: rights and first steps
items.k: Yes, if you ask. Ask as soon as you are arrested.

items.t: Can my family hire a lawyer from abroad?
items.d: Foreigner arrested in Georgia: rights and first steps
items.k: Yes. We sign the engagement remotely and step into the case right away.

items.t: How many days do I have to appeal?
items.d: Deportation from Georgia: grounds, deadlines and appeal
items.k: 10 days from when the decision is served. That is very short — contact a lawyer immediately.

items.t: Does appealing let me stay?
items.d: Deportation from Georgia: grounds, deadlines and appeal
items.k: Not on its own. An appeal does not give you a residence permit or postpone your obligation to leave.

items.t: How long can I be held in the temporary accommodation centre?
items.d: Deportation from Georgia: grounds, deadlines and appeal
items.k: 3 months, which a court can extend by 6 months — 9 months in total at most.

items.t: Who recognises a foreign decision?
items.d: Recognising a foreign court decision in Georgia
items.k: The Supreme Court of Georgia.

items.t: Does a foreign divorce always need recognition?
items.d: Recognising a foreign court decision in Georgia
items.k: No. If both spouses were citizens of the country whose authority made the decision, recognition is not needed.

items.t: Is alimony enforced automatically after recognition?
items.d: Recognising a foreign court decision in Georgia
items.k: No. Enforcement is a separate step — a lawyer plans both together.

items.t: Do I have to come to Georgia to divorce?
items.d: Divorce from abroad: without coming to Georgia
items.k: Often not. An agreed divorce can be registered at a consulate, and in a disputed case a lawyer represents you in court under a power of attorney.

items.t: I divorced abroad — is it valid in Georgia?
items.d: Divorce from abroad: without coming to Georgia
items.k: If one spouse is a Georgian citizen, the decision usually has to be recognised by the Supreme Court of Georgia.

items.t: Can I give a power of attorney online?
items.d: Divorce from abroad: without coming to Georgia
items.k: Yes, if you have a Georgian passport — with a notary in Georgia by video call, with two witnesses present.

items.t: Will they tell me the exact reason?
items.d: Refused entry to Georgia: reasons and what to do
items.k: For technical reasons — a document or a fine — usually yes. If the refusal is based on security or foreign policy, the conclusion is not reasoned by law and you often get only a general wording.

items.t: Can I appeal from abroad?
items.d: Refused entry to Georgia: reasons and what to do
items.k: Yes. A lawyer can run the case under a power of attorney while you are abroad.

items.t: Does a refusal mean I'm banned forever?
items.d: Refused entry to Georgia: reasons and what to do
items.k: Not automatically. A refusal relates to a specific attempt to enter. But if the reason isn't removed, another attempt will most likely be refused too.

items.t: Does paying the fine cancel the ban?
items.d: Overstaying in Georgia: fines and entry bans
items.k: No. Under the law, the fine and the entry ban are imposed together.

items.t: What if I don't pay the fine?
items.d: Overstaying in Georgia: fines and entry bans
items.k: Until the fine is paid, you won't be issued a visa or allowed to enter Georgia.

items.t: How long can I stay visa-free?
items.d: Overstaying in Georgia: fines and entry bans
items.k: Citizens of many countries — up to one year. The exact rule depends on your citizenship, so check in advance.

items.t: Do individual entrepreneurs need it too?
items.d: Work permit in Georgia for foreigners from 2026
items.k: Yes. A self-employed foreigner, including an individual entrepreneur, needs the right to labour activity to work in Georgia.

items.t: I have a residence permit — is that enough?
items.d: Work permit in Georgia for foreigners from 2026
items.k: Not on its own. You also need the right to labour activity, except in the cases the law exempts.

items.t: Can I apply if I have overstayed?
items.d: Work permit in Georgia for foreigners from 2026
items.k: No. You can only apply while you are lawfully in Georgia.

items.t: Can a foreigner register as an individual entrepreneur?
items.d: Individual entrepreneur in Georgia: the 1% tax for foreigners
items.k: Yes. You register at the Public Service Hall with your passport and a legal address in Georgia. Since 2026 you also need the right to labour activity to work.

items.t: What happens if income exceeds GEL 500,000?
items.d: Individual entrepreneur in Georgia: the 1% tax for foreigners
items.k: From the start of the month in which you pass the threshold until the end of the year, all your income is taxed at 3% — not just the part above the limit. Plan ahead as you get close to it.

items.t: Do I have to file every month?
items.d: Individual entrepreneur in Georgia: the 1% tax for foreigners
items.k: Yes. The declaration and the tax are due by the 15th of the following month.

items.t: When do I have to register for VAT?
items.d: Individual entrepreneur in Georgia: the 1% tax for foreigners
items.k: When your VAT-taxable transactions exceed GEL 100,000 in any 12 months — within 2 working days after that. Services to foreign clients may not count towards the amount.

items.t: Can I register as a sole trader remotely?
items.d: Individual entrepreneur in Georgia: the 1% tax for foreigners
items.k: Yes, under a notarised and apostilled power of attorney translated into Georgian. Opening a bank account usually requires attending in person.

items.t: Does a power of attorney certified at a consulate need an apostille?
items.d: Power of attorney from abroad for use in Georgia
items.k: No. A power of attorney certified by a Georgian consul is valid in Georgia without further certification.

items.t: Can a flat be sold under a power of attorney?
items.d: Power of attorney from abroad for use in Georgia
items.k: Yes, if it is certified by a notary or a consulate and clearly includes that power.

items.t: Can I revoke a power of attorney?
items.d: Power of attorney from abroad for use in Georgia
items.k: Yes, at any time. You should notify both the representative and third parties.

items.t: Is free legal aid only for criminal cases?
items.d: Free criminal lawyer in Georgia: who qualifies
items.k: No. The Legal Aid Service also helps people who can't pay in some civil and administrative cases, and gives free consultations to everyone.

items.t: Can I choose my free lawyer?
items.d: Free criminal lawyer in Georgia: who qualifies
items.k: As a rule, the Legal Aid Service appoints the lawyer. If you want to choose your lawyer yourself, you can hire a private lawyer at any stage.

items.t: Can a relative find a private lawyer for me?
items.d: Free criminal lawyer in Georgia: who qualifies
items.k: Yes. When someone is detained, it is often family members who find the lawyer. The key is to do it as quickly as possible.

items.t: Where can I check if someone is a lawyer?
items.d: How to choose a good lawyer in Georgia: 6 tips
items.k: In the Georgian Bar Association registry at gba.ge — search by first or last name. The specialisation is shown there too.

items.t: Is a lawyer (advocate) the same as a jurist?
items.d: How to choose a good lawyer in Georgia: 6 tips
items.k: No. An advocate is a member of the Bar Association and can defend you in a criminal case. A jurist has a law degree but cannot act as defence counsel in a criminal case.

items.t: Can I change lawyers during the case?
items.d: How to choose a good lawyer in Georgia: 6 tips
items.k: Yes. You can change your lawyer or hire an additional one at any stage of the case.

items.t: Does compensating the damage help?
items.d: Fraud charges in Georgia: penalties and your defence
items.k: It can affect the sentence, but it doesn't end the case automatically. Decide when and how with your lawyer.

items.t: What is the penalty for theft?
items.d: Theft charges in Georgia: penalties and your rights
items.k: Basic case — a fine, house arrest or 1 to 3 years' imprisonment. Damage over GEL 150, breaking into a home, acting as a group or a large amount make it stricter — up to 10 years.

items.t: Why does the value of the property matter?
items.d: Theft charges in Georgia: penalties and your rights
items.k: It decides which part of the article applies: over GEL 150 is significant damage, over GEL 10,000 a large amount. So checking the valuation is an important part of the defence.

items.t: I was arrested for theft. What should I do?
items.d: Theft charges in Georgia: penalties and your rights
items.k: Use your right to remain silent and ask for a lawyer. You must be charged within 48 hours, and within the next 24 hours a court decides on a preventive measure.

items.t: Who counts as a family member?
items.d: Domestic violence charges in Georgia: what to know
items.k: A spouse and children, and also parents, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren, the spouse's parents, a partner in an unregistered marriage, and a former spouse.

items.t: What is the penalty for domestic violence?
items.d: Domestic violence charges in Georgia: what to know
items.k: Community service of 80–150 hours or imprisonment of up to 2 years; with aggravating circumstances, 1 to 3 years. The court may also restrict weapons-related rights.

items.t: I'm accused. Can I contact the victim?
items.d: Domestic violence charges in Georgia: what to know
items.k: Don't — it can aggravate the charge or become a reason for detention. Comply with any order and give no statement without a lawyer.

items.t: How long will my licence be suspended?
items.d: Drunk driving in Georgia: fines, licence, prison
items.k: 0.3 to 0.7 per mille — 6 months; over 0.7 per mille — 1 year.

items.t: Can I refuse a breath test?
items.d: Drunk driving in Georgia: fines, licence, prison
items.k: Refusing is punished the same as over 0.7 per mille — a 1-year licence suspension.

items.t: When does drunk driving become a crime?
items.d: Drunk driving in Georgia: fines, licence, prison
items.k: When the drunk driver injures someone or causes a death. Driving under the influence of drugs is a criminal offence in itself.

items.t: When does the court decide on a preventive measure?
items.d: Bail or pre-trial detention in Georgia: how courts decide
items.k: Within 24 hours after the charge, which must be brought within 48 hours of arrest.

items.t: How much can bail be?
items.d: Bail or pre-trial detention in Georgia: how courts decide
items.k: Bail cannot be less than GEL 1,000. It can be money or real estate.

items.t: Can a preventive measure be appealed?
items.d: Bail or pre-trial detention in Georgia: how courts decide
items.k: Yes — once, to the Court of Appeals, within 48 hours of the ruling.

items.t: Will I have a criminal record after a plea agreement?
items.d: Plea agreements in Georgia: when they're worth it
items.k: Yes — it is a guilty verdict.

items.t: Who can propose a plea agreement?
items.d: Plea agreements in Georgia: when they're worth it
items.k: Either the accused or the prosecutor.

items.t: Can the victim appeal the agreement?
items.d: Plea agreements in Georgia: when they're worth it
items.k: No, but the victim keeps the right to file a civil claim. The prosecutor must consult the victim before the agreement.

items.t: I was arrested over drugs. Do I have to make a statement?
items.d: Arrested for drugs in Georgia: what to do
items.k: No — you have the right to remain silent and the right to a lawyer from the moment of arrest.

items.t: I disagree with the record. What should I do?
items.d: Arrested for drugs in Georgia: what to do
items.k: Don't sign it, or add a note. Watch who is present at the search, what is taken and how it is packed.

items.t: What is the fine for a small amount of marijuana?
items.d: Marijuana law in Georgia: what gets you fined?
items.k: GEL 500 — it is an administrative offence.

items.t: What is the fine for using it in public?
items.d: Marijuana law in Georgia: what gets you fined?
items.k: On the street, in parks, cafés, transport and other public places — GEL 800–1,200; in front of minors or near schools — GEL 1,000–1,500.

items.t: When is it a criminal offence?
items.d: Marijuana law in Georgia: what gets you fined?
items.k: For more than a small amount (over 5 grams of dried marijuana), giving it to someone (even for free), bringing it into or out of Georgia, or growing the plant.

items.t: What should I do first?
items.d: Unfairly dismissed in Georgia? What to do
items.k: Ask your employer for the written grounds for dismissal, and keep every document and message.

items.t: What can I claim in court?
items.d: Unfairly dismissed in Georgia? What to do
items.k: Reinstatement, pay for the period you were forced out of work, or compensation if reinstatement is impossible or you don't want it.

items.t: Should I sign a 'voluntary resignation'?
items.d: Unfairly dismissed in Georgia? What to do
items.k: Not under pressure — it is one of the most common mistakes. Deadlines to challenge a dismissal are short, so contact a lawyer soon.

items.t: Within what time must I accept an inheritance?
items.d: Accepting an inheritance in Georgia from abroad
items.k: Within 6 months of its opening — as a rule, the date of death.

items.t: Do I need to come to Georgia?
items.d: Accepting an inheritance in Georgia from abroad
items.k: No — you can act by power of attorney: at an embassy or consulate, with a local notary, or, if you have a Georgian passport, online with a notary in Georgia.

items.t: I was scammed online. What should I do first?
items.d: Scammed online? How to try to get your money back
items.k: Contact your bank immediately to block the card and dispute the payment. Then change your passwords and keep all the evidence.

items.t: Can the money be recovered?
items.d: Scammed online? How to try to get your money back
items.k: Sometimes — especially if you contact the bank quickly or the offender is identified.

items.t: Should I trust a 'money recovery' service?
items.d: Scammed online? How to try to get your money back
items.k: No. Services that promise to recover your money for an upfront fee are, as a rule, another scam.

items.t: Where do I appeal a fine?
items.d: How to appeal a fine in Georgia
items.k: Depending on the type — to a superior body or in court. Where and by when is usually stated in the decision itself.

items.t: When does the appeal deadline start?
items.d: How to appeal a fine in Georgia
items.k: From the day you received the decision. Note that date — the deadline is short.

items.t: What evidence will I need?
items.d: How to appeal a fine in Georgia
items.k: Photos and video, witnesses' contacts, receipts, tickets, permits — anything that supports your position.

items.t: What should I check in the Public Registry extract?
items.d: Buying an apartment in Georgia: what to check
items.k: Who the owner is, the size of the apartment, and whether there is a mortgage, seizure or prohibition. Get an up-to-date extract.

items.t: Is the spouse's consent needed?
items.d: Buying an apartment in Georgia: what to check
items.k: If the apartment was bought during a marriage, the spouse's consent may be needed. If there are several owners, all must agree.

items.t: When does the apartment become mine?
items.d: Buying an apartment in Georgia: what to check
items.k: Ownership arises on registration with the Public Registry. Until then, the apartment isn't legally yours.

items.t: What do I need to register an LLC?
items.d: Registering an LLC in Georgia: what you need
items.k: A company name, details of the partners and director, a charter, and a legal address in Georgia with the owner's consent.

items.t: How long does registration take?
items.d: Registering an LLC in Georgia: what you need
items.k: Usually one business day at the Public Registry. The company is registered as a taxpayer at the same time.

items.t: Can a foreigner set up an LLC?
items.d: Registering an LLC in Georgia: what you need
items.k: Yes — foreign individuals and companies can be the sole partner and director.

items.t: What types of residence permit are there?
items.d: Residence permits in Georgia: which type do you need?
items.k: Mainly: work, business, property, family, study and investment.

items.t: Where do I apply?
items.d: Residence permits in Georgia: which type do you need?
items.k: At the Public Service Hall.

items.t: Why are applications often refused?
items.d: Residence permits in Georgia: which type do you need?
items.k: Choosing the wrong type is a common reason. A refusal can be appealed — deadlines are short.

items.t: Is a court order needed for a search?
items.d: Police search in Georgia: your rights and what to do
items.k: As a rule, yes. In urgent cases a search can be done without one, but a court then checks whether it was lawful.

items.t: Can I call a lawyer during a search?
items.d: Police search in Georgia: your rights and what to do
items.k: Yes — you can contact a lawyer and ask them to come.

items.t: What are my rights regarding the record?
items.d: Police search in Georgia: your rights and what to do
items.k: To read it, add comments, get a copy, and have every seized item listed.

items.t: Is there a fixed percentage for alimony?
items.d: Child support (alimony) in Georgia: how the amount is set
items.k: No — Georgian law sets no fixed percentage. The amount is set by agreement or by the court.

items.t: What does the court consider?
items.d: Child support (alimony) in Georgia: how the amount is set
items.k: The child's age and needs, both parents' income and assets, and any duty to support other people.

items.t: Who pays alimony?
items.d: Child support (alimony) in Georgia: how the amount is set
items.k: As a rule, the parent who doesn't live with the child.

items.t: How long can I be held?
items.d: Detained in Georgia? Your rights and what to do
items.k: You must be charged within 48 hours and brought before a court within the next 24 hours.

items.t: I can't afford a lawyer. What then?
items.d: Detained in Georgia? Your rights and what to do
items.k: In cases provided by law, a lawyer is appointed at the state's expense.

items.t: I don't speak Georgian. Do I get an interpreter?
items.d: Detained in Georgia? Your rights and what to do
items.k: Yes — you have the right to a free interpreter.

items.t: When does a court decide the divorce?
items.d: Divorce in Georgia: civil registry or court?
items.k: When one spouse doesn't agree, or there is a dispute over where the child lives, alimony or property.

items.t: Who will the child live with?
items.d: Divorce in Georgia: civil registry or court?
items.k: The parents agree on this; in a dispute, the court decides in the child's best interests.

items.t: What courts are there in Georgia?
items.d: Who is a judge? Courts and judges in Georgia
items.k: The Constitutional Court and the common courts. The common courts are the district (city) courts, the courts of appeals and the Supreme Court.

items.t: What does the Supreme Court hear?
items.d: Who is a judge? Courts and judges in Georgia
items.k: Cassation appeals against decisions of the courts of appeals — it is the highest and final instance.

items.t: What does a judge do?
items.d: Who is a judge? Courts and judges in Georgia
